channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Ramzan Kadyrov Re-elected as Head of Chechnya with 99.85% of Votes
item.description: Ramzan Kadyrov secured 99.85% of the votes in the Chechen Republic's head election, according to the Central Election Commission. This marks his third term leading the region since 2007. Kadyrov previously won with 99.7% in 2021 and 97.94% in 2016. Two other candidates received less than 0.05% of the vote.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Reduces Number of Pensioners Receiving Below Minimum Pension
item.description: In Kyrgyzstan, the percentage of pensioners receiving less than the minimum pension has decreased from 37% to 5% as of June 2026. The minimum pension will increase from 7,100 soms to 8,800 soms starting October 2026, aligning with constitutional requirements.

item.title: Uzbekistan President reviews Karakalpakstan's development initiatives since 2017
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev visited Karakalpakstan to assess development projects initiated in 2017. The focus is on economic growth linked to social problem-solving and future confidence. The visit highlighted efforts to address challenges stemming from the Aral Sea's drying, including soil salinization, health risks, and job scarcity.

item.title: Tajikistan's petroglyphs and historical sites added to UNESCO tentative list
item.description: Five petroglyph complexes in Tajikistan's Gorno-Badakhshan region and four historical-natural sites in Khatlon region have been inscribed on UNESCO's tentative list. These sites, dating from the Mesolithic to the Middle Ages, represent valuable cultural heritage significant for studying ancient civilizations and regional development.

item.title: Russian State Duma elections held in Uzbekistan with CIS observers present
item.description: Voting for the Russian State Duma elections concluded in Uzbekistan on September 20. Polling stations operated in Tashkent, Fergana, and Samarkand, with international observers from the CIS mission monitoring the process. The CIS mission was the largest international observer group for these elections.

item.title: Uzbekistan May Invest $200 Million in Railway Modernization
item.description: Uzbekistan is considering a $200 million investment to modernize its railways. The funds would aim to increase the capacity of several key sections, including Maktaaral-Sirdaryo and Angren-Pop, by 25-30 percent.

item.title: Tajikistan shares 'One Health' approach experience at FAO conference
item.description: Tajikistan presented its national experience in ensuring food security and developing sustainable production systems at the FAO Global Conference on 'One Health' in agro-food systems. The conference, held in Rome from September 21-23, focuses on practical applications of the 'One Health' approach to enhance food security, production resilience, and resource management.

item.title: Bishkek ranks 461st globally in Oxford Economics' 2026 Global Cities Index
item.description: Bishkek climbed 37 places to rank 461st out of 1,000 cities in the 2026 Global Cities Index by Oxford Economics. The Kyrgyz capital performed best in human capital (194th) and ranked 383rd for economics. Among Central Asian capitals, Bishkek ranked below Astana (281st) and Tashkent (343rd), but above Dushanbe (672nd).

item.title: Kyrgyzstan sees significant reduction in pensioners receiving below-minimum pensions
item.description: In Kyrgyzstan, the number of pensioners receiving less than the minimum pension has drastically decreased. As of June 2026, only 5% of pensioners receive below the minimum, a significant drop from 37% previously. Starting October 2026, the minimum pension will increase to 8,800 som, aligning with constitutional requirements.

item.title: Four arrested in Chirchiq, Uzbekistan for operating a drug laboratory
item.description: Four individuals have been apprehended in Chirchiq, Tashkent region, for allegedly operating a drug laboratory in a rented apartment. The State Security Service reported that the suspects were producing and selling hashish oil, using materials supplied by foreign curators via Telegram.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Introduces New Registration Rules for Foreigners and Stateless Persons
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has updated its registration rules for foreigners and stateless individuals. The new procedure aims to streamline registration, clarify document and address requirements, and establish uniform rules for various categories of foreign citizens, including specific provisions for extending stays.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's security service disrupts Afghan hashish smuggling route
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's State Committee for National Security (SCNS) has disrupted a drug trafficking route smuggling Afghan hashish via Tajikistan. Two Kyrgyz nationals were detained on suspicion of involvement. A criminal case was initiated for illegal drug trafficking, with additional charges for violence against family members for one suspect.

item.title: Dushanbe to host first meeting of Asian Parliamentary Assembly committee
item.description: Dushanbe will host a meeting of the Permanent Committee on Social and Cultural Affairs of the Asian Parliamentary Assembly from September 24-27, 2026. Over 20 member states are expected to attend, including representatives from the UAE, Saudi Arabia, China, Iran, Kyrgyzstan, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, and Russia. Tajikistan holds the chairmanship for 2026-2027.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan MP questions Bishkek's traffic congestion solutions, suggests metro or moratorium
item.description: A Member of Parliament in Kyrgyzstan questioned the effectiveness of current measures to combat traffic jams in Bishkek. He suggested considering a moratorium on new high-rise construction within the city or exploring the possibility of building a metro system. Similar issues were noted in Osh.

item.title: Kazakh prosecutor tells Chechen activist he may become a martyr
item.description: A Chechen activist, Mansur Movlayev, has attempted suicide twice after Kazakhstan's Cassation Court denied him refugee status. A prosecutor reportedly told him, "You can become a martyr. This is your trial."

item.title: Tajikistan presents child rights report to UN Committee in Geneva
item.description: Tajikistan's delegation, led by the Justice Minister, presented its periodic national report to the UN Committee on the Rights of the Child in Geneva. The report detailed the country's progress in implementing the Convention on the Rights of the Child.

item.title: Ghuliston mayor promises Adrasmon mining plant to resume operations in September
item.description: The mayor of Ghuliston has pledged that the Adrasmon ore processing plant will restart operations in September. The reasons for the plant's previous shutdown are being investigated. The plant was established in the second half of the 20th century.

item.title: Uzbekistan Launches Monitoring of Cotton Harvesters' Labor Conditions
item.description: Uzbekistan will monitor cotton harvesters' labor conditions from September 25 to October 31 to ensure no child or forced labor is used. A 65-member monitoring group, including labor inspectors and NGO representatives, will conduct checks. Hotlines and reporting channels are available.

item.title: Man suspected of embezzling 5 billion soums extradited from Turkey to Uzbekistan
item.description: A man, S.A., wanted internationally for allegedly embezzling 5 billion soums by misappropriating credit funds, has been apprehended in Turkey and returned to Uzbekistan. The Istanbul Consulate reported the extradition. He faces charges under Article 167 of the Criminal Code.

item.title: President Mirziyoyev's visit to Karakalpakstan spurs new development projects
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev's visit to Karakalpakstan marks a significant step for the region's development. Projects worth $7.6 billion have been launched, focusing on economic diversification, industrial growth, and job creation. Regional GDP has surged from 8.5 trillion soums in 2016 to over 54 trillion soums.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Loan Portfolio Exceeds 644 Trillion Soums, Growing by 68 Trillion in One Year
item.description: The total loan debt of the population and businesses to banks in Uzbekistan has surpassed 644.63 trillion soums. This figure represents an increase of 68.4 trillion soums over the past year, indicating significant growth in lending.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Establish World-Class Cell Technology Center for Advanced Research and Treatment
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to build a world-class cell technology center to become a global hub for advanced cell-based research, production, and patient treatment. The initiative aims to elevate the country's capabilities in regenerative medicine.

item.title: Tajik Court Sentences Man to 22 Years for Stabbing Police Major
item.description: A 27-year-old man has been sentenced to 22 years in prison in Tajikistan's Sughd region for stabbing a police major. The incident occurred on May 12 near the Syr Darya river in Khujand. The officer, who intervened in a dispute, was stabbed multiple times but recovered and returned to duty.

item.title: Uzbekistan Banks Prevent Over 18 Million Fraudulent Transactions
item.description: Uzbekistan's banks prevented over 18 million fraudulent transactions in the first half of 2026. Antifraud and antivirus systems also cleaned malware from 2 million devices. Further details are available online.

item.title: Moscow Faces Mass Drone Attack on Election Day; Ballistic Missile Mentioned
item.description: Moscow experienced a mass drone attack on election day, with reports suggesting the use of a "Pelican" ballistic missile. Several facilities, including an oil refinery, sustained significant damage. Further details are available online.

item.title: Latvian President: Most NATO States Cannot Repel Russian Missile Attacks
item.description: The Latvian president stated that most NATO countries cannot repel Russian missile attacks. He highlighted significant challenges in European and NATO air defense. Russia may attempt to advance on the front lines during winter. Further details are available online.

item.title: Uzbekistan Places Businessman Mominjon Yuldashev on International Wanted List
item.description: Uzbekistan has placed businessman Mominjon Yuldashev, from the Fergana region, on the Interpol wanted list. He is sought for embezzlement under Article 167 of the Criminal Code. Yuldashev has previously been involved in business dealings in Belarus and had sanctions imposed by the World Bank.

item.title: Chinese investor discovers 4 tons of gold reserves in Uzbekistan's Karakalpakstan
item.description: A Chinese investor has identified 4 tons of gold reserves on 200 hectares of land in Karakalpakstan, Uzbekistan, following a $33 million investment. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev announced plans to expand geological exploration and establish a gold mining and processing cluster creating 1,000 jobs.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's National Bank removes "Zolotaya Korona" from electronic money systems registry
item.description: The National Bank of Kyrgyzstan has canceled the registration of the Russian payment system "Zolotaya Korona" based on the operator's request. The system, registered in Kyrgyzstan in 2016, also operates as an international money transfer operator. Eight registrations have been annulled this year.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Social Fund Reports Surplus but Faces Budget Dependence
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Social Fund reported a surplus of approximately 3 billion soms for 2025, with revenues around 130 billion and expenses 127 billion. However, 44.4 billion soms came from the state budget, indicating significant dependence. Pensioner purchasing power decreased due to rising prices.

item.title: Kyrgyz President visits Utah Olympic Park, studies winter sports development
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov visited Utah Olympic Park during his US trip. He met with the 2034 Winter Olympics organizing committee chair and learned about sports infrastructure development and legacy use. Japarov noted Utah's experience is valuable for Kyrgyzstan's winter sports potential.

item.title: Emomali Rahmon begins working trip to Sughd region
item.description: Tajikistan's President Emomali Rahmon arrived in the Sughd region for a working trip on September 20. The visit aims to open new facilities, assess the socio-economic situation, meet residents, and participate in events marking the 35th anniversary of Tajikistan's independence. The trip focuses on state development and economic progress.

item.title: Interpol identifies 126 terrorists using AI in Operation Shams II
item.description: Interpol has identified 126 foreign fighters through the use of artificial intelligence (AI) during anti-terrorism Operation Shams II. The operation, led by Interpol with specialists from 11 countries, analyzed over 108,000 images shared by jihadists. AI tools helped remove duplicates and enhance image quality, reducing the dataset for facial recognition.

item.title: Uzbekistan allocated 18.3 trillion soums in mortgage loans over 8 months
item.description: In Uzbekistan, 18.3 trillion soums were allocated for mortgage loans in the first eight months of the year. Approximately 74% of these loans were for the primary market. Data also revealed the age distribution of loan recipients and the proportion of men and women among them.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan faces growing pension burden as contributors decline
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is experiencing a decrease in insurance premium contributors while the number of pensioners rises, according to Social Fund data. The ratio has fallen to 1.8 contributors per pensioner, raising concerns about budget strain. The real purchasing power of pensions has also declined despite an increase.

item.title: Seven detained after mass brawl outside Osh nightclub
item.description: Police detained seven individuals following a mass brawl outside the '03222' nightclub in Osh. The incident occurred on A. Masaliev Street and video footage circulated on social media. One participant, born in 2004, sustained injuries and sought medical attention. An investigation is underway.

item.title: Iran Submits Peace Proposal to US via Qatar to End Conflict
item.description: Iran has sent its proposal to the United States aimed at ending the ongoing conflict. The peace initiative was conveyed to Washington through Qatari mediation. A response from the US is currently awaited.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Meets Utah Governor and Senate Leadership in US Visit
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov met with Utah Governor Spencer Cox and Senate leadership in Salt Lake City. Discussions focused on Kyrgyz-American cooperation, particularly in economic, investment, and cultural spheres, including mining and tourism.

item.title: Central Asian Glaciers Are Disappearing, Study Finds
item.description: Glaciers in Central Asia are diminishing, according to a study by World Meteorological Organization scientists examining the last five years. Water inflow into reservoirs in Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, Kyrgyzstan, and Afghanistan has significantly decreased.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan extends bonus payments for doctors, addresses textbook shortages
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's government is providing compensation payments to doctors in deficit specialties across most of the country, excluding Bishkek and Osh. Monthly stipends are also available for interns and residents training outside major cities. Meanwhile, a shortage of school textbooks has led to high prices, with the state printing house denying allegations of illegal book diversion.
